canonical_name: Radon-Nikodym theorem (exact measure category and formulation open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 测度的绝对连续与密度函数
literal_source_claim_en: Absolute continuity of measures and density functions.
statement_blocker: The catalogue gloss does not select positive versus signed, complex, or vector measures; finite, sigma-finite, s-finite, localizable, or abstract decomposition hypotheses; the orientation of the measures; existence versus iff; density codomain, measurability, integrability, or finiteness; equality-of-measures versus set-integral form; or almost-everywhere uniqueness. The matching 1930 source scan is not transcribed and independently reviewed. domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix a measurable space, the measure category and codomain, finiteness or decomposition hypotheses, measure orientation, density quotient convention, every Lean universe and typeclass, and any signed or vector scalar structure.
conclusion: Prospective family only: absolute continuity of one measure with respect to another yields, or is equivalent to, representation by a measurable density, possibly with almost-everywhere uniqueness. Exact direction and representation are open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve zero measures, an empty measurable space, infinite densities, null reference measure, non-sigma-finite examples, equality versus almost-everywhere equality, and any signed or vector zero-variation cases.

formal_candidates_not_credited.candidate_type_summary: absolute continuity implies equality with the rnDeriv-weighted reference measure under HaveLebesgueDecomposition

formal_candidates_not_credited.candidate_type_summary: for a signed measure s and sigma-finite positive reference measure mu, vector-measure absolute continuity is equivalent to s being the signed density measure of s.rnDeriv mu
